answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed radio relay on a remote mesa, reached across a real bridge the operator must photograph. One relay per operator, inspected in person each season, its telemetry logged publicly; random checks summon the holder to key that relay on camera within minutes, so one operator cannot staff two relays at once. A vine of local subscribers vouches for the service, and the license fee in outside money doubles per relay on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real relay, another climb, another operator, and twice the prior fee.
